newsitem.title: USA: Penn Traffic debt off on weaker earnings.
newsitem.headline: Penn Traffic debt off on weaker earnings.

text.p: Penn Traffic Co debt fell on Monday following news of a drop in first quarter revenues, high-yield traders said.
"Penn paper fell after the weak report," said one trader of distressed debt. "Penn 9-5/8's were bid off 1-1/2 points at 52-3/4 bid, 53-1/4 offer," he said.
The company's 8.625 percent notes were quoted off one point at 81 bid, 82 offer, while the supermarket's 10-1/4, 10-3/8 and 11-1/2 percent paper traded off 1/2 point, traders said.

Penn Traffic reported an 8.3 percent decline in its first quarter revenues of $759.4 million compared to $827.7 million a year ago. The company said same store sales were off 8.1 percent for the 13 weeks ended May 3 versus the same period last year.
"The sales decline prevented us from achieving our short-term profit goals for the quarter," said Phillip E. Hawkins, President and Chief Executive Officer of Penn Traffic, in a press release.
"Our gross margins improved modestly during the first quarter, versus the prior year, as a result of merchandising programs implemented last year, particularly in the perishables area," Hawkins said.
"This was accomplished at the same time that we significiantly expanded pricing and merchandising initiatives in selective markets," he said.
Hawkins said Penn Traffic is implementing a number of near-and intermediate-term intiatives to address the continued sales decline.

In April, Moody's Investors Sevice Inc downgraded the company's senior note rating to B3 from B2 and affirmed the Caa rating on the firm's subordinated debentures. At the same time, Moody's assigned a B1 rating to Penn Traffic's $250 million secured bank credit facility.

Moody's cited the ongoing slide in Penn Traffic's comprable store sales, which has led to declining operating cash flow, weakened debt protection measures, as well as the effective subordination of the senior notes to the secured bank facility.
Penn Traffic also reported that its bank credit agreement has been ammended to modify certain financial covenants.
"This ammendment demonstrates the ongoing support of our bank group for the company," said Martin A. Fox, Vice Chairman of Finance.
Standard & Poor's rates Penn Traffic's senior unsecured debt at single-B and subordinated debt at CCC-plus.
Meanwhile, corporate bond players are said to be awaiting results of this morning's conference call between the company and industry analysts.
The Penn Traffic Company operates 265 supermarkets in Pennsylvania, upstate New York, Ohio and West Virginia.
